content:
alex: Heads-up: we’re seeing intermittent Prometheus prober failures in us-west2 starting ~09:07 UTC. p95 scrape latency spiked to ~4s and a bunch of DNS lookup timeouts in the exporter logs. remote_write queue length climbed on the write-side for a few minutes. Anyone on call can triage?

priya: I see alerts firing on prober-scrape-latency and remotewrite-buffered-queue in datadog. Linking grafana panel: https://grafana.example.com/d/abcd/probes?orgId=1&from=now-30m .

jamie: grabbing logs from the prober pods now. Initial grep shows repeated name resolution failures to kube-dns: 
```
level=warn ts=2026-03-17T09:07:23Z caller=scrape.go:312 msg="DNS lookup error" host="gpu-exporter-usw2.internal" err="lookup gpu-exporter-usw2.internal on 10.10.0.10:53: read udp 10.240.0.5:41769->10.10.0.10:53: i/o timeout"
```

elyse: Could be node-level network flakiness; we had a kube-proxy rolling restart earlier today in that cluster. Any kernel drops or CNI errors?

priya: checked k8s events on the affected nodes: some transient NetworkUnavailable events during 09:05-09:10, and a handful of kube-dns restarts.

alex: Ops-bot, did the automated DNS failover run?

ops-bot: Automated DNS healthcheck detected high latencies for 10.10.0.10:53 between 09:03–09:11 UTC and switched to secondary 10.10.1.10 at 09:12 UTC. No TTL exceed recorded. :robot_face:

jamie: After the DNS switch, scrape latency returned to normal but we still saw a small backlog on remote_write until 09:18. Remote_write error snippets: 
```
level=error ts=2026-03-17T09:08:41Z caller=client.go:210 msg="write failed" err="context deadline exceeded" queued=412
```

priya: Looks like the prober relabel config might be creating lots of distinct target labels for a few exporter pods during failures. Current relabel snippet: 
```
- action: replace
  source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_gpu_model, __meta_kubernetes_pod_name]
  target_label: gpu_id
```

elyse: That could expand cardinality if pod_name is ephemeral and probes retry rapidly. Maybe change to stable label (node) or drop pod_name during scrapes for prober job.

alex: Agreed — short-term: add a relabel rule to drop pod_name for prober job and reduce target churn. Medium-term: add retry/backoff on DNS resolution in prober (config flag) and make remote_write accept a slightly longer buffer.

jamie: I pushed a temporary relabel override to the prober job in staging config: `relabel_configs: - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_gpu_model] target_label: gpu_model` will avoid pod_name. Rolling out to canary now.

priya: Monitoring panels show canary is clean. I'll open a small infra task to evaluate kube-dns HA in us-west2 and to audit other scrape jobs for label cardinality risks.

elyse: Also propose tuning the prober alert: only alert if p95 > 2s AND remotewrite queue > 200 for 5m to reduce noise from transient dns blips.

alex: Sounds good. Action items: priya -> infra task (kube-dns HA), jamie -> relabel fix rollout to prod after canary, elyse -> alert refinement PR, ops-bot -> note incident in incident channel.

ops-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-331, severity: low, brief: Prober DNS timeouts caused transient scrape latency and remote_write backlog in us-west2. Remediated by DNS failover and relabel canary.

priya: Closing the immediate issue, will follow-up with postmortem draft on Monday. :thumbsup:
